answer: Partition identity space into sixty-four registries by address hash, deposit scaled by registry share: crowding fakes into one grove raises its share, so each puppet pays base times share ratio; scattering spreads the same penalty across every delta. Deposits lock thirty days and early exit forfeits half; auditors replay three random registries each epoch, checking balances and locks. A hundred fakes either crowd one registry into unaffordable deposits or dilute control across sixty-four wharf registries on equal audit odds, keeping verification cheap while cost grows with concentration.
